prompt: After months of progress, a runner has one terrible race and wants to quit her training plan entirely. Which response is best supported by the evidence of her own record?

options.text: Quit, because the latest result is always the truest one
Double training volume immediately to make up for the race
Ignore the race completely and never analyse it
Treat one race as one data point: check the months-long trend and any race-day factors, then adjust one thing if the data suggests it

explanation: A single bad performance, influenced by sleep, weather or illness, does not outweigh a trend. Reviewing the record calmly separates a blip from a real pattern worth changing.
